summary: The root فجو (fjw) primarily means to open or widen. It describes opening a door, widening the space between legs, or the string of a bow being raised.
lane: 1 فَجَا بَابَهُ ذ , (K,) [aor. يَفْجُو ,] inf. n. فَجْوٌ , (TA,) He opened his door. (K.) -b2- And فَجَا القَوْسَ , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) He raised the string of the bow [or made it distant ] from the part called its كَبِد : (S, K:) and so فَجَّهَا . (S and K in art. فج .) -b3- And فَجَا رِجْلَيْهِ , or مَا بَيْنَ رِجْلَيْهِ , He parted his legs wide, or straddled; or did so to make water: and so فَجَّ . (TA in art. فج .) -A2- فَجِيَتْ , (S, K, TA, [in the CK, and in one of my copies of the S, erroneously, فَجِئَت ,]) aor. تَفْجَى , inf. n. فَجًا , (S, TA,) The bow had its string raised [or distant ] from the part called its كَبِد ; (S, K;) and so . (ISd, TA.) -b2- And فَجِىَ , [in the CK, erroneously, فَجِئَ ,] aor. as above, (K, TA,) and so the inf. n., i. e. فَجًا , (K, * TA,) He (a man, TA) was wide between the thighs, or between the knees, or between the shanks. (K, TA.) [And it is implied in the S * and K that it is also said of a camel, meaning He was wide between the hocks. ] -b3- And فَجِيَتْ said of a she-camel, inf. n. فَجًا , She was, or became, large in the belly: (K, TA:) mentioned by ISd, but with an expression of uncertainty as to its correctness. (TA.)

headwords.def: أَفْجَى an epithet, of which the fem. is فَجْوَآءُ . (K, TA.) The latter, applied to a bow, Having its string distant from the part called its كَبِد ; (S, K, TA;) as also ; and so فَجَّآءُ [mentioned in art. فج ]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) And the former, (K, TA,) applied to a man, (TA,) Wide between the thighs, or between the knees, or between the shanks: or, applied to a camel, wide between the hocks: (K, TA:) or, accord. to Az, it signifies having the thighs very wide apart. (TA.) [ Freytag adds “ Ventrosus, ” applied to a camel, as from the K, in which I do not find it.] [Accord. to the TA, some of the words of this art. have ى for the final radical; but for this distinction there is no reason.]
